Mating-pad refs (those starting with 'P_') anchor at (0,0) automatically and are listed here only when they need explicit rotation or face. Future scope: locked trace segments (smash doesn't model traces yet).

U_HACC.reason: H3LIS331 ±400g high-G accel: deliberately offset 1.0/1.0 mm (= 1.41 mm radius) from the spin axis so its centripetal term a = ω²r is a usable, non-zero spin-rate readout (≈20 g at 60 Hz, ≈228 g at 200 Hz) — the only roll/ω sensor that survives both spin rates, since the ISM330 gyro saturates (>4000 dps) and the IIS2MDC mag is sub-Nyquist at 200 Hz. The 1.41 mm radius is small enough to stay inside ±400 g even at 200 Hz worst case and to dominate the unspecified intrinsic MEMS proof-mass offset (DS9012 does not give it), yet keeps the axial rapid-deceleration reading clean (centripetal lands on X/Y; <5% cross-axis bleed is negligible vs the rapid deceleration). Characterise r_eff empirically (spin at known ω → r_eff=√(a/ω²)). Moved to fin_ble_board's TOP face 2026-11-17 (user: activation_interface's top too busy) at the same 1.41 mm offset — fin_ble's bottom centre is U_G0B1_FIN; the axial readings don't care which board. UPDATE 2026-11-16: the 1.41 mm offset saturates ±400 g above ≈16,000 rpm (≈14,000 rpm → ≈310 g OK; 50,200 rpm saturates X/Y at ANY achievable radius — r would have to be ≤0.14 mm). High-spin rate/roll therefore comes from a dedicated fast AMR/TMR turn-counting magnetometer (user decision, part TBD); the H3LIS stays for axial >16 g (drag, ejection, parachute opening) and as the low-spin ω cross-check.
